solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dog from Alabama rested near Paisley perhaps

blocks.note: AL is the postal abbreviation for the US state
past tense of sit, to rest
Ian Paisley, the Northern Irish politician, supplies the first name

explanation.surface: A dog has come from Alabama and is lying down beside someone called Paisley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' flags Paisley as one example of a man named Ian; Ian Paisley was a famous Northern Ireland politician and preacher.
explanation.definitionFit: An Alsatian is a breed of dog, the British name for the German shepherd.

clue.text: Bill firm over road agreement

blocks.note: AC, short for account, a bill to be paid
CO is the abbreviation for company
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A company's invoice for road works leads to a settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' simply places the first pieces above the road abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An accord is a formal settlement or treaty between parties, a synonym of agreement.

clue.text: Air outside a Queen's garment

indicators.note: one word standing outside others wraps around them on both sides

blocks.note: an air is a tune or song
taken as written
R for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: The outdoor air surrounds a queen's piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' looks like the atmosphere, but here it is a melody; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarong is a wrapped cloth worn round the waist in South-East Asia, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Bloc (no outsiders) with euro cents in circulation?

definitions.text: Bloc (no outsiders) with euro cents in circulation?

indicators.note: removing the outsiders strips the first and last letters, leaving only the middle
things in circulation move around, so these letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: the inner two letters of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trading group whose member states use euro coins.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg form the Benelux bloc and all use euro cents.
explanation.definitionFit: The Low Countries are Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg, a regional grouping all of whose members adopted the euro currency.

clue.text: Strange story covered by article

indicators.note: something covered by another thing sits inside it, wrapped on both sides

blocks.note: a lie is a made-up story
AN is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An odd tale is reported in a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a newspaper item, but it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien as an adjective means foreign or unfamiliar, hence odd or unusual.

clue.text: Ready money graduate's banked in African city quarter

indicators.note: money banked in an account is deposited inside it

blocks.note: ready money is cash in hand
a Bachelor of Arts graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate deposits cash in a bank somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', and the graduate is placed inside the money word.
explanation.definitionFit: A casbah is the old walled citadel area of a North African city such as Algiers.

clue.text: Rue, as mama (decent) playing here?

indicators.note: letters playing about are moving freely and can fall into any order

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the punctuation

explanation.surface: A respectable mother regrets the gambling her children do at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as definition: a proper mum might rue her children playing slot machines at such a place.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement arcade is a hall of coin-operated games and slot machines, found on British seafronts.

clue.text: Card game in vehicle going North over California desert

indicators.note: in a down clue, travelling north means reading upwards, from the bottom

blocks.note: a cab is a taxi
CA is the postal abbreviation for the US state
to rat is to desert or betray one's side

explanation.surface: People play cards in a car as it heads up through the Californian desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a sandy waste but is the verb meaning to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a casino card game in which players bet on which hand comes closest to nine.

clue.text: Being experienced, ran across lair

indicators.note: stretching across something means spanning it on both sides

blocks.note: to hare is to run fast
an animal's den is its lair

explanation.surface: A seasoned animal dashes across its lair.
explanation.walkthrough: The run verb wraps the lair word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardened means toughened by long practice, seasoned and inured, as an experienced person is.

clue.text: Philanthropist has worry about Geordie soldier

indicators.note: about means around, so one word surrounds the others

blocks.note: care as anxiety or concern
a Geordie comes from Newcastle, in North East England
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A generous benefactor frets over a soldier from Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is a native of Tyneside in North East England, giving the compass abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Carnegie, the steel magnate, gave away most of his fortune to found libraries and trusts.

clue.text: Fruit appliance Jack used at first with reserve and resistance

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the preceding word only

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
the first letter of the word
ice as coolness, reserve of manner
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget that Jack first used along with reserve power and resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: Reserve here is the noun for an aloof manner, which is icy.
explanation.definitionFit: A juicer is a kitchen device that extracts juice from fruit.

clue.text: Hit small three-wheeler

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a trike is a tricycle

explanation.surface: Someone struck a little tricycle.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike someone or something is to hit it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Musical form welcomed by matron, dowager

indicators.note: letters welcomed by other words are taken in and sit within them

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A piece of music is received warmly by a stately matron.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical composition in which a principal theme returns between contrasting episodes.

clue.text: Church record about left-wing American

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word encloses what follows

blocks.note: to note is to record
a red is a socialist or communist
AM is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A church keeps records about a left-leaning American.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre Dame is the famous Gothic cathedral in Paris, a church dedicated to Our Lady.

clue.text: Showing care to be in legal position in box

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other

blocks.note: onside is a player's lawful position in football
a crate is a wooden box

explanation.surface: Being thoughtful means a defendant standing in the dock in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legal position' sounds like a courtroom term but is football's rule about where an attacker may stand; 'box' suggests the witness box.
explanation.definitionFit: A considerate person shows thought and kindness for the feelings of others.

clue.text: Smarter to ignore current idle talk

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out of consideration, so it is dropped

blocks.note: nattier means more smartly dressed
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: It is wiser to tune out the trendy chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smarter' tempts as cleverer; it means better dressed. Remove the current symbol from that word to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To natter is to chat casually, and as a noun it is aimless chit-chat.

clue.text: Crazy joke – Cockney woman's

blocks.note: a crack is a wisecrack, a joke
Cockneys drop their aitches, so the woman's possessive loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A mad gag belongs to a woman from London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech, from East London, drops the H sound, so the possessive 'hers' becomes 'ers.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackers is British slang for mad or insane.

clue.text: He gets top quality college paper at end of year

indicators.note: at end of points to the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: A is a first-class grade
C is the abbreviation for college
a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A top student from college receives a paper at the close of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: A quire is an old measure of paper, a twentieth of a ream.
explanation.definitionFit: An acquirer is one who obtains or gains possession of something.

clue.text: Taking on current time when travelling

indicators.note: letters that are travelling are on the move and so rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Hiring staff at the present moment while on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Recruitment is the hiring of new staff, the act of engaging employees.

clue.text: Passage of water, not curved, we're told

indicators.note: what we are told reaches us by ear, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: something not curved is straight

explanation.surface: A channel of the sea is said to run without bends.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow channel of sea joining two larger bodies of water.

clue.text: Promote development of forest after replanting

indicators.note: replanting puts the trees back in new positions, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Encourage woodland growth once the trees have been planted again.
explanation.definitionFit: To foster something is to encourage or nurture its growth.

clue.text: Very many – fifty, received by titled lady

indicators.note: something received by a person is taken in, ending up inside

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
a countess is a noblewoman

explanation.surface: A noblewoman is handed a vast number, fifty of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Countless means too numerous to count, innumerable.

clue.text: Find the answer, the one and only – very impressed!

indicators.note: impressed means pressed into something, so one letter is set inside

blocks.note: sole means single, the only one
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A solver cracks a clue and is greatly delighted at being the only one to do so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impressed' reads as admiring but means pressed in.
explanation.definitionFit: To solve is to work out the solution to a problem or puzzle.

clue.text: Relationship in troika disturbed after Kelvin leaves

indicators.note: once the kelvin unit has left, its letter is gone from the word
disturbed things are thrown out of their settled order

blocks.note: taken as written
K is the symbol for the kelvin

explanation.surface: A three-person team's relationship falls apart once Kelvin walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: Kelvin looks like a person's name but is the temperature unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is the quantitative relation between two amounts.

clue.text: Listen in every afternoon – radio (wireless) is good to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with means taking only the opening letter of each word

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the six words

explanation.surface: Someone tunes in each afternoon to the wireless, which is a good habit.
explanation.walkthrough: Earwig as a verb is informal British for eavesdropping, not the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To earwig is British slang for eavesdropping on a conversation.

clue.text: Nice bird swapping tips on hotel

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends, its first and last letters
swapping means one letter goes out and another comes in its place

blocks.note: a game bird
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A lovely bird is exchanging tip-offs about a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of 'hotel' are swapped: its H in the bird becomes its L.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice and pleasant are synonyms for agreeable or enjoyable.

clue.text: Emphasis is very French aboard vessel

indicators.note: something aboard a ship is carried inside it

blocks.note: très is French for very
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Stress is very French on board ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is the emphasis placed on a syllable or point, a direct synonym.

clue.text: He chooses reader following directions

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the second-named word is placed first in the answer

blocks.note: south and east, two compass points
a lector reads lessons aloud in church

explanation.surface: The person who picks the team is a reader taking instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: A lector is a church reader; the compass points come first because the reader follows them.
explanation.definitionFit: A selector picks members of a sports team, someone whose job is choosing.
